verses.author: model_A
verses.text: A boat leaves the harbor before anyone is awake to see it go.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
The water keeps no record of which way it went —

only the gulls remember, and they aren't telling.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
Something in their circling
looks like a question with no one left to ask —

so they land, and fold the answer under one wing.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
Morning finds the dock unbothered by any of this,

still holding the rope's loop
where the boat used to argue with the tide.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
The loop waits anyway,

patient as a mouth
that has forgotten what it meant to say.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
Somewhere a knot remembers being tied

by hands that are elsewhere now, doing
something with their fingers that isn't this.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
The rope keeps the shape

of a promise no one asked it to keep —
useful, useless, holding on regardless.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
I let go of things faster than rope does,

and still find my hands
curled around nothing, hours later.
